title: Event Loop and Call Stack
description: Understand the JavaScript event loop, call stack, and task queue.

options.text: setTimeout(fn, 0) guarantees fn executes immediately after the current function
options.explanation: setTimeout(fn, 0) puts fn in the macrotask queue. It executes after the current call stack clears AND any pending microtasks (Promises) complete. It's not immediate.

options.text: Microtasks (Promise.then) execute before macrotasks (setTimeout) when both are queued
options.explanation: After each macrotask, the engine drains the entire microtask queue before picking up the next macrotask. Promise callbacks are microtasks; setTimeout callbacks are macrotasks.

options.text: JavaScript can execute multiple functions simultaneously on different threads
options.explanation: JavaScript is single-threaded — it has one call stack and executes one thing at a time. Web Workers provide separate threads but don't share the main thread's scope or DOM access.

options.text: The event loop only processes events when the call stack is empty and there are no pending microtasks
options.explanation: The event loop processes macrotasks one at a time from the task queue when the call stack is empty. Between macrotasks, ALL pending microtasks are processed. The statement is partially right but 'no pending microtasks' is misleading.
